title: visStatistics 0.2.0
text: Unified normality testing across branches. two-group case (t-test vs Wilcoxon) multi-group case (ANOVA vs Kruskal-Wallis) now share normality test: shapiro.test() applied internally studentized residuals lm(y ~ x) via rstandard(). Variance homogeneity test changed bartlett.test() levene.test(). Levene-Brown-Forsythe test (using median) robust non-normality Bartlett’s test. test now determines whether Student’s t-test (t.test(var.equal = TRUE)) Welch’s t-test used two-group case, whether aov() oneway.test() used multi-group case. Large-sample threshold changed 30 50 per group. every group exceeds 50 observations, normality testing skipped parametric tests applied directly (justified central limit theorem). Post-hoc test selection. oneway.test() (Welch’s ANOVA) used unequal variances, games.howell() appropriate post-hoc test, assume equal variances. TukeyHSD() remains aov() (Student’s ANOVA). Spearman-correlation. new correlation branch (do_regression = FALSE) uses Spearman rank correlation exclusively. Spearman’s rho Pearson’s r applied ranks: yields nearly identical results bivariate normal data requires distributional assumptions. separate Pearson branch implemented, Pearson correlation requires bivariate normality — condition reliably tested marginal distributions alone.

title: visStatistics 0.2.0
text: Formula interface: visstat(y ~ x, data = df) now supported alongside existing visstat(x, y) visstat(dataframe, "namey", "namex") forms.
